rounds.text: Rane (Madras) Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at an attractive P/E of 15.98x against a sector benchmark of 25.2x [E6], alongside a compelling EV/EBITDA of 6.86x compared to the sector's 12.91x [E11]. This undervaluation stands in stark contrast to phenomenal long-term compounding, featuring 10-year sales growth of 16% [E14], 5-year sales growth of 27% [E15], and an astonishing 99% profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E21]. Furthermore, fundamentals are actively outpacing stock price appreciation, with 5-year profit growth reaching 43% against a price growth of 24% [E56]. The business generates robust cash, demonstrated by an operating cash flow of Rs 221 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 88 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36], backed by a stellar 100 relative-strength rating against the Nifty 500 [E51] and a rules-based screen score of 88 out of 100 [E61]. Conceded: the stock trades at 4.02x its book value [E2] and three-year compounded profit growth sits at -5% [E20].

The bull cites a cheap P/E of 15.98x against the sector [E6], but omits that the stock trades at 27.5x on a standalone trailing basis [E1] and carries a high price-to-book ratio of 4.02x [E2]. While the bull highlights phenomenal profit growth [E21], it glosses over the severe medium-term contraction where compounded profit growth over 3 years sits at -5% [E20], which correctly triggers a screen warning for decelerating earnings growth [E66]. Conceded: the company achieved Rs 221 Cr in operating cash flow and Rs 88 Cr in free cash flow [E35, E36]. However, this cash generation is shadowed by an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend [E32, E33] alongside promoters quietly trimming their stake from 72.65% to 70.45% [E41]. Finally, the bull leans heavily on historical momentum [E51], ignoring the sobering reality of a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -85.8% and high annualized volatility of 48.3% [E53, E54].
